turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Good morning. Nothing eventful to report, really — pretty standard night for me.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Around 10:30, like most nights. Woke up briefly around 1am but that wasn't from settling in, that was a callout text.
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?
About 6 and a half hours, give or take. I'd say decent, not great — the callout woke me up and I was stuck thinking for a while before I dropped off again, but the front end of the night was solid.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? Why did you choose to do that activity?
Read a few more chapters of the thriller I've got going — same paperback I've been chipping away at for a while. It's just my wind-down routine, doesn't take much thought.
That sounds interesting. What’s the title of the thriller you’re reading?
"Line of Fire" — some ex-military guy chasing down a conspiracy. Nothing highbrow, just something to shut my brain off with.

Thanks for sharing that. 

What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

Two weeks of nights, one callout, no callout — over the past two weeks the callouts have probably had the biggest effect. Even when they're brief, getting yanked out of sleep and lying there thinking for a while afterward adds up. Otherwise it's been pretty routine — same bedtime, same wake-up.
Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your sleep and callouts?
Pretty typical, yeah. Callouts run maybe twice a month, so this wasn't out of the ordinary — just happened to land last night. Nothing's really changed on my end.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

Yeah, mostly. Six and a half hours with one interruption isn't going to keep me up at night worrying about it — the routine's solid and I feel fine most days. The callouts are just part of the job, not something I need to fix.
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?
7-9 hours would be nice, but it's just not realistic with a 7am start and callouts thrown in. I get by fine on six or six and a half, so I don't lose sleep over the number, if you'll pardon the pun.
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep?

Routine's the main thing — same bedtime, same wake time, doesn't leave much room for it to go wrong. What makes it hard is the job, honestly: fixed shift means I can't just sleep in to make up for a callout, so those nights I just eat the short sleep and move on.
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?
Not really — I'll check it if there's a work call I'm expecting, but otherwise I leave it charging in the other room. Old habit more than anything, just makes it easier to actually fall asleep.
Do you regularly use social media? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
Not really, no — I'll scroll through it earlier in the evening sometimes, but I'm not the type to lie in bed with it going. It's not much of a habit for me, honestly.
Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications)?
"Not really, no. I've poked around with one out of curiosity, but it's not something I use day to day."

Thanks for explaining that.

If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

"Probably sleeping through those callout nights without the hour of lying there overthinking it. I can't do much about the phone going off, but the tossing and turning after is the part I'd cut if I could."

Thanks, that’s clear.

Now a few quick background questions. You can skip anything you’d rather not share.

What is your age?
52. Just turned it in June, if it matters.
Thank you. What is your profession?
Municipal water-utility technician. I deal with pipes, mains, that kind of thing — mostly day shifts, but I get called out at odd hours sometimes when something bursts.
Thanks. What is your country of birth?
"Here originally, actually — I've lived in this city eight years, but I'm not from around here. Grew up a few hundred miles away, still get the odd word wrong in local slang."
Thanks. And your current country of residence?
"Here, same as where I live and work."
Thank you. And roughly how many years ago did you move to your current city, if you’re comfortable sharing?
